clue.text: It may save one cast beside fiery pit

definitions.text: It may save one cast beside fiery pit

parts.words: It may save one cast beside fiery pit
parts.note: surface reading: a rescuer pulling someone thrown down next to a burning hole in the ground
setter's reading: the cast are actors on stage, and the pit is the theatre's orchestra stalls, where a fire might break out

explanation.surface: Someone flung beside a blazing pit is saved from danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like a verb meaning thrown, but it is the company of actors, and the pit is part of the auditorium.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatres must lower a fireproof screen between stage and auditorium so flames cannot spread from one to the other.

clue.text: Play providing part on the boards

parts.note: to part is to divide or split apart
boards and tables are both flat surfaces for meals; 'on' places this after the first piece

explanation.surface: Taking a role in a stage production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the boards' looks like a theatre idiom, matching 'Play', but here boards are simply tables.
explanation.definitionFit: Terence Rattigan wrote a well-known 1954 drama of that title, set in a seaside hotel dining room.

clue.text: Score twice, since score went missing

parts.note: 'for' can mean because or since

indicators.note: something that has gone missing is no longer there, so the word named just before vanishes from the longer word

parts.note: a score is twenty

explanation.surface: A team scored two goals after a previous effort was lost.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'went' itself is removed from TWENTY, leaving TY; the clue uses 'went' both as the letters to delete and as part of the deletion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Two lots of twenty make the number between thirty-nine and forty-one.

clue.text: Watch line that's a feature of American parade

parts.note: ticker is old slang for a watch, from its ticking
a tape is a line, as at the finish of a race

explanation.surface: A wristwatch strap or line that marchers in a US procession display.
explanation.definitionFit: New York celebrations shower returning heroes with paper streamers from office windows, giving the procession its name.

clue.text: It's used in bridge building, and is thus encased in tin

indicators.note: something encased sits inside a shell, so the preceding words go inside the metal word

parts.note: a can is a tin
taken as written
so means in this way, thus

explanation.surface: A bridge-building component that comes packaged inside a metal box.
explanation.definitionFit: Engineers sink a watertight chamber into a riverbed so workers can lay foundations for piers underwater.

clue.text: Having a list of very rich?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: of a ship, leaning and swaying from side to side

explanation.walkthrough: 'List' suggests a written roll of names, like a rich list; here it is a ship's lean.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel that heels over is said to be swaying this way, and informally someone flush with cash is described with the same word.

clue.text: Painful account, horribly heartless

parts.note: AC is the standard abbreviation for account

indicators.note: without a heart means the whole middle is taken out, leaving only the two ends of the word

parts.note: only the first and last letters are kept

explanation.surface: A cruel, unfeeling report that is painful to hear.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a body that hurts or is sore, the shorter being a milder, informal term.

clue.text: Various tensions about Times following equal opportunities policy

indicators.note: various suggests many different forms, so the following word's letters are rearranged
about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the newspaper's symbol

parts.note: rearranged
X is the multiplication sign, read as 'times'

explanation.surface: Strains around The Times newspaper after it adopted a fair employment policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper this crossword appears in, but it is the multiplication symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: An employer treating men and women alike in hiring and pay is practising gender fairness, avoiding discrimination by sex.

clue.text: Not leaving after an argument, perhaps

definitions.text: Not leaving after an argument, perhaps

parts.words: Not leaving after an argument, perhaps
parts.note: surface reading: someone who stays put rather than storming out after a row
setter's reading: not leaving money or property in a will, as a parent might do after a family quarrel

explanation.surface: A person refusing to walk out after a heated quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaving' reads as departing; the setter means bequeathing.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting a relative out of one's will means deliberately bequeathing them nothing, often after a family feud.

clue.text: Girl's back, getting stuck into the bottle in local

indicators.note: being stuck into something puts it inside, so the name goes within the word for a small bottle

parts.note: a phial is a small glass bottle

indicators.note: going back means the girl's name is read from its end to its start

parts.note: Cora is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl turns her back and hits the drink at her neighbourhood pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' is British for a neighbourhood pub, which fits the bottle; here it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Something relating to a church district, or narrow in outlook, is confined to a small neighbourhood.

clue.text: This capital Cockney pronounces bother

indicators.note: a Londoner's accent drops the opening H, so the word is judged by how it is said in that accent

parts.note: to bother is to annoy; drop the H from the city's name, Cockney-style, and it is said the same way

explanation.surface: Asking how an East Londoner says a certain city, as if it were a bother.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class East London accent, famous for dropping H at the start of words.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the seat of government of Vietnam, so it is a national capital.

clue.text: Keats and Yeats did, but don't

definitions.text: Keats and Yeats did, but don't

parts.note: surface reading: two poets who wrote verse; setter's reading: the names Keats and Yeats share their ending sound
setter's reading: the words 'but' and 'don't' fail to match in sound

explanation.surface: Two famous poets did something in their verse which the reader is told not to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'But don't' sounds like an instruction; it is the pair of words 'but' and 'don't', which do not sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Words match in this way when their final sounds are the same, as the two poets' surnames do.

clue.text: Avoid refuse collector

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to miss out or dodge
second meaning: a large open bin for builders' rubbish

explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse collector' suggests a dustman; in Britain the word also names a big metal waste container, a dumpster.
explanation.definitionFit: One can dodge a class by missing it, and the British name for a large rubbish container left on a street is the same word.

clue.text: Sulphur discharge cut — reduced by half, for a start

definitions.text: reduced by half, for a start
definitions.note: a prefix, meaning half, placed at the start of words such as semi-skimmed

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the word for discharge loses its final letter

parts.note: S is the chemical symbol for sulphur
to emit is to discharge or give off

explanation.surface: Factory emissions of sulphur were cut, halving them at first.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes a word beginning rather than a whole word: the prefix that means half.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin-derived prefix halves what follows, as in semicircle, so it sits at the beginning of words.

clue.text: Star performer's right in depiction of holy Virgin Mary

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for right inside the short word for holy

parts.note: pi is informal shorthand for pious, holy
R is the abbreviation for right
the Madonna is a title of the Virgin Mary, especially in paintings and statues of her

explanation.surface: A leading singer claims to have the right to appear in a religious painting of the Virgin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holy Virgin Mary' reads as one phrase, but 'holy' is split off for PI.
explanation.definitionFit: The leading female singer in an opera company is its star, and the term also covers any temperamental lead.

clue.text: Type of Oriental letter set in metal

indicators.note: set in means mounted inside, as a jewel in a ring, so the letter goes within the metal

parts.note: tin is a metal
beta is the second letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A typeface with Eastern letters cast in metal type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Type' and 'letter set in metal' suggest printing; type here means kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from the Himalayan region north of Nepal is one kind of Asian, the 'Oriental' of older usage.

clue.text: Keep out of club one golfers don't play with!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to vote against admitting someone as a member
second meaning: golf balls are white, so a dark-coloured one is never used

explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' and 'golfers' together suggest a golf club; the first meaning is about membership ballots.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of clubs once voted by dropping a white or dark token into a box, a dark one rejecting the candidate.

clue.text: Set off, sharing trip

indicators.note: to trip is to stumble, so the preceding word's letters tumble into a new order

parts.note: every letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: Leaving on a journey together with others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set off' looks like departing, which suits a trip; it means to enhance by decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: A cook decorates a dish with parsley or lemon to show it off, which is to set it off.

clue.text: Leader of team knocked in a corner

indicators.note: the leader is the one at the front, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: first letter only
to rap is to knock sharply

explanation.surface: A team captain is knocked down in a corner of the pitch or ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cornered has no way out, which is the same as being caught with escape cut off.

clue.text: More than one machine starts to develop electrical faults

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so only the first letter of each of the next two words is used

parts.note: first letter only
first letter only
vices are faults or failings

explanation.surface: Several machines begin to develop electrical faults.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faults' looks electrical, but here it means moral failings.
explanation.definitionFit: Gadgets and appliances are pieces of equipment, the plural covering several mechanical contrivances.

clue.text: Domestic pet putting meat back, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word for back loses its final letter

parts.note: ham is a meat
the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A household pet has nearly all of its meat put back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like an instruction to return the meat; it is the noun for a ship's rear.
explanation.definitionFit: This small burrowing rodent with cheek pouches is a common caged companion animal.

clue.text: From which a drawer needs to pull out easily

definitions.text: From which a drawer needs to pull out easily

parts.words: From which a drawer needs to pull out easily
parts.note: surface reading: a chest of drawers whose drawer must slide out smoothly
setter's reading: a drawer is someone who draws a gun

explanation.surface: A piece of furniture whose drawer must slide out smoothly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawer' reads as part of a desk; it is a gunslinger who draws.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunfighter carries a pistol in a leather case on the hip, and a quick draw needs it to come free smoothly.

clue.text: Fire poet overlooking line

indicators.note: to overlook is to leave out, so the poet's name drops the abbreviation for line

parts.note: William Blake was an English poet
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Sacking a poet who has skipped a line of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' suggests dismissal or flames; it is the potter's sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Potters harden clay by heating it in a kiln, which is called firing, much as bread is cooked in an oven.

clue.text: Return of potentially shocking corruption

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: a live wire carries current and can give a shock

explanation.surface: A scandal that may cause outrage comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shocking' suggests scandal; it is electrical.
explanation.definitionFit: Wickedness and moral depravity are both forms of wrongdoing, the noun naming badness in general.

clue.text: Small amount of earth? Violet's turned in a small amount

indicators.note: in places the turned name inside the word for a tiny quantity

parts.note: a dot is a tiny amount

indicators.note: turned round means the short form of the name is read backwards

parts.note: Vi is the usual short form of the name Violet

explanation.surface: Violet has turned over a little bit of soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small amount of earth?' could be a pinch of soil; the question mark flags the golfing sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf club hacks out a chunk of turf with a swing, a small piece of ground that players replace.

clue.text: Some deliver socialism — the left

indicators.note: some means only a part, so the answer is a run of letters within the next words

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Some political parties promise to bring socialism, and that is the Left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The left' looks political, matching socialism; it means the left-hand page of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: In printing, the back of a leaf is the left-hand page of an open book, opposite the recto.

clue.text: Doctor inexplicably disliked skin

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the subject of the rhyme 'I do not like thee, Doctor ..., the reason why I cannot tell'

explanation.surface: A doctor who is mysteriously unpopular, perhaps with his patients.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half needs a 17th-century English nursery rhyme by Tom Brown about a doctor he could not explain his dislike for.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme's Doctor was a real Oxford dean, and an older word for an animal hide or pelt is the same.

clue.text: Remove Times before completion of puzzle

parts.note: eras are periods of time

indicators.note: completion is the end, so only the final letter of the next word is used

parts.note: last letter only

explanation.surface: Taking The Times away before the crossword has been finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like this newspaper; it is plural periods.
explanation.definitionFit: To rub out writing or delete data is to wipe it away, leaving no trace.

clue.text: Shun an interminable boozer — get away quickly

indicators.note: interminable here means without an end, so the word for boozer loses its final letter

parts.note: to cut someone is to ignore or snub them
taken as written
a drunk is a heavy drinker

explanation.surface: Advice to dodge a bore who drinks without end and escape fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boozer' is also British slang for a pub, which tempts; here it is a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to flee abruptly, originally of a ship slashing its anchor rope to escape.

clue.text: Similar role e'd transformed in opera

indicators.note: something transformed has changed its form, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: all thirteen letters are used

explanation.surface: A comparable part, edited, appears in an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd "e'd" is there only to supply the letters E and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Donizetti's comic Italian work of 1832, whose title means The Elixir of Love, is a well-known stage piece for singers.
